hindi: तुम उपयाम से ग्रहण किए गए हो; आदित्यों के लिए तुम्हें। हे विष्णु, हे उरुगाय, यह तुम्हारा सोम है; उसकी रक्षा करो; वे तुम्हें हानि न पहुँचाएँ।
english: You are taken with the upayāma; you for the Ādityas. O Viṣṇu, O wide-going one, this is your Soma; guard it; let them not harm you.
notes: upayāma is an obscure ritual term, left untranslated. dabhan is read as a 3 pl. aorist injunctive with prohibitive mā; the subject is not stated. urugāya is rendered as the epithet 'wide-going'.

english: O Indra, you are never barren; you do not hold back from the offerer. O bounteous one; more and more indeed is joined the gift of you, the god. You for the Ādityas.

hindi: हे विवस्वान्, हे आदित्य, यह तुम्हारा सोमपान है; उसमें आनन्द लो। हे मनुष्यो, इस वचन में श्रद्धा रखो: जब आशीर्वाद देने वाले दम्पती वांछित को प्राप्त करते हैं, तब पुरुष पुत्र उत्पन्न होता है, वह धन पाता है और तब निर्दोष होकर प्रतिदिन घर में समृद्ध होता है।
english: O Vivasvat, O Āditya, this is your Soma-drinking; delight in it. O men, place your trust in this speech: when the two lords of the house, bestowers of blessing, obtain the desirable, a male son is born, he finds wealth, and then, faultless, he thrives in the house every day.
notes: Line 2 is hard: 'yad āśīrdā dampatī vāmam aśnutaḥ' is rendered with yad as 'when', āśīrdā as an adjective of the pair ('bestowers of blessing') and vāma as 'the desirable'; the construction is uncertain. The text speaks of 'the two lords of the house' (dampatī) without naming them; arapaḥ is read 'faultless' (a-rapas). Vivasvat and Āditya are two vocatives as printed and are not further identified.

hindi: तुम उपयाम से ग्रहण किए गए हो। हे देव सोम, बृहस्पति द्वारा निचोड़े गए तुम्हारे बिन्दु के बलयुक्त और पत्नियों वाले ग्रहों को मैं पाकर समृद्ध होऊँ। मैं ऊपर से हूँ, मैं नीचे से हूँ; जो अन्तरिक्ष है, वही मेरा पिता हुआ। मैंने सूर्य को दोनों ओर से देखा; मैंने देवों के उस परम को देखा जो गुहा में है।
english: You are taken with the upayāma. O god Soma, of you, the drop pressed by Bṛhaspati, may I prosper in the cups that have power and are accompanied by wives. I am from above, I am from below; what is the midspace, that became my father. I saw Sūrya on both sides; I saw the highest of the gods, which is in secret.
notes: Obscure in several places. bṛhaspatisutasya is taken as 'of the one pressed by Bṛhaspati', agreeing with indoḥ/Soma; ta indor is read te indoḥ 'of you, the drop'. ṛdhyāsam with accusative grahān is read as 'may I prosper in/through' (uncertain construction); the mark ~2 on grahān is a printed nasal/length sign. Line 3, 'devānāṃ paramaṃ guhā yat', is read 'the highest of the gods, which is in secret' (aham dadarśa governs it). Antarikṣa is rendered 'midspace'.

english: You are the expiation of the sin made by the gods; you are the expiation of the sin made by men; you are the expiation of the sin made by the fathers; you are the expiation of the sin made by oneself; you are the expiation of sin upon sin. And whatever sin I have done knowing, and whatever not knowing, of all that sin you are the expiation.
notes: avayajana (ava-yajana) is rendered 'expiation' (literally a sacrificing-away). enasa enaso is read 'of sin upon sin'. 'yac cāham eno vidvāṃś cakāra yac cāvidvāṃs tasya' is read as 'the sin which I did knowing, and which not knowing, of that'. The mark ~ on vidvā~ś and avidvā~s is a printed nasal sign. The English of the last sentence follows the Sanskrit order.

hindi: हम तेज के साथ, दूध के साथ, शरीरों के साथ, मन के साथ, कल्याणकारी के साथ मिल गए हैं। उदार दाता त्वष्टा धन का वितरण करें, और शरीर का जो ढीला-बिछुड़ा है, उसे पोंछ दें।
english: We have come together with splendour, with milk, with bodies, with mind, with the kind one. May Tvaṣṭṛ, the generous giver, distribute riches, and may he wipe over whatever is loosened of the body.

Unit 16 repeats this text.

english: O Indra, bring us together with mind, with cows, with patrons, O bounteous one, with well-being; together with brahman, and with whatever is made by the gods; together in the favour of the gods worthy of sacrifice. Svāhā.

hindi: समुद्र में तुम्हारा हृदय है, जलों के भीतर। तुममें ओषधियाँ और जल प्रविष्ट हों। हे यज्ञपति, यज्ञ के सूक्त-कथन में और नमः-वाक् में हम तुम्हारी सेवा करें, यत्। स्वाहा।
english: In the ocean is your heart, within the waters. May plants and waters enter you. O lord of the sacrifice, in the saying of the sūkta and the utterance of homage of the sacrifice, may we serve you, yat (sense uncertain). Svāhā.
notes: yajñasya is read with the two locatives ('of the sacrifice'). yat is left untranslated; its use here is uncertain. oṣadhi is rendered 'plant'.
lines_deva: स॒मु॒द्रे ते॒ हृद॑यम॒प्स्वन्तः सं त्वा॑ विश॒न्त्वोष॑धीरु॒ताप॑ः
य॒ज्ञस्य॑ त्वा यज्ञपते सू॒क्तोक्तौ॑ नमोवा॒के वि॑धेम॒ यत्स्वाहा॑

ya̱jñasya̭ tvā yajñapate sū̱ktoktaṷ namovā̱ke vi̭dhema̱ yatsvāhā̭

hindi: हे दिव्य जलो, यह तुम्हारा गर्भ है; उसे भली-भाँति प्रसन्न, भली-भाँति धारित करके धारण करो। हे देव सोम, यह तुम्हारा लोक है; उसमें कल्याण को बढ़ाओ और चारों ओर बढ़ाओ।
english: O divine waters, this is your embryo; bear him, well pleased and well borne. O god Soma, this is your world; in it increase well-being and increase all around.
notes: vakṣva is read as an imperative of √vakṣ 'grow, be strong'; it could also be √vah 'carry' (vakṣva as future-imperative), which would give 'bear well-being and bear around'. The first reading is used (uncertain). devīr āpaḥ is read as a vocative address; the embryo is not identified. śam is taken as the accusative object of vakṣva (uncertain).
lines_deva: देवी॑राप ए॒ष वो॒ गर्भ॒स्तᳪ  सुप्री॑त॒ᳪ सुभृ॑तं बिभृत
देव॑ सोमै॒ष ते॑ लो॒कस्तस्मि॒ञ्छं च॒ वक्ष्व॒ परि॑ च॒ वक्ष्व॑

deva̭ somai̱ṣa tḙ lo̱kastasmi̱ñchaṃ ca̱ vakṣva̱ pari̭ ca̱ vakṣva̭

hindi: हे अवभृथ, हे निचुम्पुण, तुम निचेरु हो, निचुम्पुण। देवों के साथ मैंने देवों द्वारा किए गए पाप को शान्त किया; मनुष्यों के साथ मनुष्यों द्वारा किए गए पाप को शान्त किया। हे पुरुरावन् के देव, हानि से रक्षा करो। तुम देवों की समिधा हो।
english: O avabhṛtha, O Nicumpuṇa, you are nicēru, Nicumpuṇa. With the gods I have appeased the sin made by the gods; with mortals the sin made by mortals. O god of Pururāvan, protect from harm. You are the kindling-stick of the gods.
notes: Very obscure: nicumpuṇa, nicēru and pururāvṇaḥ are kept untranslated (pururāvṇo deva is rendered 'O god of Pururāvan', uncertain). ayāsiṣam (ava-√yā) is read 'I have appeased'; other renderings are 'I have averted, removed'. avabhṛtha is the final bath (a ritual term kept as 'avabhṛtha'). samit is read 'kindling-stick' (samidh).
lines_deva: अव॑भृथ निचुम्पुण निचे॒रुर॑सि निचुम्पु॒णः
अव॑ देवैर्दे॒वकृ॑त॒मेनो॑ऽयासिष॒मव॒ मर्त्यै॒र्मर्त्य॑कृतं पुरु॒राव्णो॑ देव रि॒षस्पा॑हि
दे॒वाना॑ᳪ  स॒मिद॑सि

ava̭ devairde̱vakṛ̭ta̱meno̭'yāsiṣa̱mava̱ martyai̱rmartya̭kṛtaṃ puru̱rāvṇo̭ deva ri̱ṣaspā̭hi

hindi: दस मास का गर्भ जरायु के साथ हिले। जैसे यह वायु चलती है, जैसे समुद्र हिलता है, वैसे ही यह दस मास का गर्भ जरायु के साथ छूटा।
english: Let the ten-month embryo move together with the afterbirth. As this wind moves, as the ocean moves, so this ten-month one was released together with the afterbirth.
notes: asraj is read as a form of √sṛj 'was released' (the exact form, aorist passive or injunctive, is uncertain). The word and the line break after 'saha' are as printed. The subject is the embryo as stated; nothing more is added.
lines_deva: एज॑तु॒ दश॑मास्यो॒ गर्भो॑ ज॒रायु॑णा स॒ह । यथा॒ऽयं वा॒युरेज॑ति॒ यथा॑ समु॒द्र एज॑ति
ए॒वा॒यं दश॑मास्यो॒ अस्र॑ज्ज॒रायु॑णा स॒ह

e̱vā̱yaṃ daśa̭māsyo̱ asra̭jja̱rāyṷṇā sa̱ha

hindi: जिसके लिए तुम्हारा यज्ञ के योग्य गर्भ है, जिसके लिए सुनहरी योनि है; जिसके अंग अवक्र हैं, उसे मैंने माता से मिला दिया है। स्वाहा।
english: She for whom your embryo is worthy of sacrifice, for whom the womb is golden; him whose limbs are unbent I have united with the mother. Svāhā.
notes: yasyai is a dative form of the relative (the construction 'to whom ... the embryo' is read loosely as 'she for whom'). ahrutā is read 'unbent, not crooked' (a-hruta), uncertain. The text does not say who the mother or the embryo is.
lines_deva: यस्यै॑ ते य॒ज्ञियो॒ गर्भो॒ यस्यै॒ योनि॑र्हिरण्यी
अङ्गा॒न्यह्रु॑ता॒ यस्य॒ तं मा॒त्रा सम॑जीगम॒ᳪ स्वाहा॑

aṅgā̱nyahrṷtā̱ yasya̱ taṃ mā̱trā sama̭jīgama̱ᳪ svāhā̭

hindi: बहुत आश्चर्यों वाला, नाना रूपों वाला, बिन्दु, धीर, भीतर महिमा को आलिप्त कर चुका है। लोक एकपदी, द्विपदी, त्रिपदी, चतुष्पदी, अष्टापदी के पीछे फैलें। स्वाहा।
english: Rich in wonders, of various forms, the drop, the wise one has anointed the greatness within. May the worlds spread out after the one-footed, the two-footed, the three-footed, the four-footed, the eight-footed. Svāhā.
notes: Obscure. ānañja is read 'has anointed' (ā-√añj), with mahimānam as object; the sense 'has made manifest' is also possible. induḥ is rendered 'drop'. The five feminine numerals (ekapadī ... aṣṭāpadī) are accusative as printed but the verb prathantām is plural imperative, so bhuvanā (worlds) is read as the subject and the five accusatives as what the worlds follow (anu); what they refer to is not stated and is not added.
lines_deva: पुरुद॒स्मो विषु॑रूप॒ इन्दु॑र॒न्तर्म॑हि॒मान॑मानञ्ज॒ धीर॑ः
एक॑पदीं द्वि॒पदीं॑ त्रि॒पदीं॒ चतु॒ष्पदीम॒ष्टाप॑दीं॒ भुव॒नानु॑ प्रथन्ता॒ᳪ  स्वाहा॑

eka̭padīṃ dvi̱padī̭ṃ tri̱padī̱ṃ catu̱ṣpadīma̱ṣṭāpa̭dī̱ṃ bhuva̱nānṷ prathantā̱ᳪ  svāhā̭

hindi: हे मरुतो, स्वर्ग के महान तेज वाले, जिसके निवास में तुम रक्षा करते हो, वह मनुष्य सर्वोत्तम रक्षित है।
english: O Maruts of heaven, of great glory, he in whose dwelling you give protection is the best protected man.
notes: pāthā is read as √pā 'protect'; √pā 'drink' is also possible ('in whose dwelling you drink'). divaḥ is read 'of heaven' with vimahasaḥ. The quality of the order of the clause is as printed.
lines_deva: मरु॑तो॒ यस्य॒ हि क्षये॑ पा॒था दि॒वो वि॑महसः । स सु॑गो॒पात॑मो॒ जन॑ः

hindi: महान द्यौ और पृथ्वी हमारे इस यज्ञ को सींचें; पोषणों से हमें भरपूर करें।
english: May great heaven and earth sprinkle this our sacrifice; may they fill us with nourishments.
notes: mimikṣatām is read 'may they sprinkle, moisten' (desiderative of √mikṣ, uncertain). bharīman is rendered 'nourishment' (bearing, bringing). mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca is read as two nouns with a dual adjective.
lines_deva: म॒ही द्यौः पृ॑थि॒वी च॑ न इ॒मं य॒ज्ञं मि॑मिक्षताम् । पि॒पृ॒तां नो॒ भरी॑मभिः

hindi: हे वृत्र का वध करने वाले, रथ पर चढ़ो; तुम्हारे दोनों हरित घोड़े पवित्र वचन से जोते गए हैं। कूटने का पत्थर अपनी ध्वनि से तुम्हारे मन को भली प्रकार हमारी ओर करे। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए।
english: Mount the chariot, O slayer of Vṛtra; your two bay horses are yoked by the sacred utterance (brahman). May the pressing stone, with its sound, turn your mind well toward us. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin. This is your seat; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin.
notes: Line 1 is a Ṛgvedic-type verse; line 2 is the formula of the Ṣoḍaśin cup, with no verb for 'you for Indra' (nothing supplied). 'upayāma-gṛhīta' rendered literally; upayāma is left untranslated. hari = bay horses; the line itself says only 'two bays'. vagnu = sound/call (possibly 'cry'). The final -a of ṣoḍaśina before eṣa is the pausal Vedic sandhi of ṣoḍaśine.
lines_deva: आ ति॑ष्ठ वृत्रह॒न्रथं॑ यु॒क्ता ते॒ ब्रह्म॑णा॒ हरी॑ । अ॒र्वा॒चीन॒ᳪ  सु ते॒ मनो॒ ग्रावा॑ कृणोतु व॒ग्नुना॑
उ॒प॒या॒मगृ॑हीतो॒ऽसीन्द्रा॑य त्वा षोड॒शिन॑  ए॒ष ते॒ योनि॒रिन्द्रा॑य त्वा षोड॒शिने॑

hindi: लम्बे केशों वाले, कक्ष्या भरने वाले बलवान दोनों हरित घोड़ों को जोतो। फिर, हे सोम पीने वाले इन्द्र, हमारे गीतों के श्रवण को प्राप्त हो। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए।
english: Yoke the two long-maned bay stallions, who fill the girth. Then, O Indra, drinker of Soma, come to hear our songs. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin. This is your seat; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin.
notes: 'upaśrutim cara' rendered 'come to hear'; 'kakṣya-prā' (filling the girth) is obscure and rendered literally. 'naḥ' taken as 'our' with girām (could also be 'for us'). Token 'girāmupaśrutim' is a single token, so the split shows girām + upa-śrutim in one token.
lines_deva: यु॒क्ष्वा हि के॒शिना॒ हरी॒ वृष॑णा कक्ष्य॒प्रा । अथा॑ न इन्द्र सोमपा गि॒रामुप॑श्रुतिं चर
उ॒प॒या॒मगृ॑हीतो॒ऽसीन्द्रा॑य त्वा षोड॒शिन॑  ए॒ष ते॒ योनि॒रिन्द्रा॑य त्वा षोड॒शिने॑

u̱pa̱yā̱magṛ̭hīto̱'sīndrā̭ya tvā ṣoḍa̱śina̭  e̱ṣa te̱ yoni̱rindrā̭ya tvā ṣoḍa̱śinḙ

hindi: दोनों हरित घोड़े अजेय बल वाले इन्द्र को ही ऋषियों की स्तुतियों और मनुष्यों के यज्ञ के पास ले जाते हैं। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए।
english: The two bay horses carry Indra indeed, of unassailed strength, to the praises of the sages and to the sacrifice of men. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin. This is your seat; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin.

hindi: जिससे बढ़कर कोई दूसरा उत्पन्न नहीं हुआ है, जो सब भुवनों में प्रविष्ट हुआ है, वह प्रजापति प्रजा के साथ आनन्दित होता हुआ तीन ज्योतियों का सेवन करता है; वही षोडशी है।
english: Than whom no other, higher one has been born, who has entered all the worlds: that Prajāpati, delighting with offspring, attends the three lights; he is the Ṣoḍaśin.
notes: 'yasmān na jātaḥ paro anyaḥ asti' is literally 'from whom no other beyond is born'; the order of the relative clauses is kept as in the verse. 'saṃrarāṇaḥ' (from sam-√rā) is rendered 'delighting', but 'bestowing' is possible; 'sacate' = attends/follows (could also be 'is joined to'). The three 'lights' are not named in the line.
lines_deva: यस्मा॒न्न जा॒तः परो॑ अ॒न्यो अस्ति॒ य आ॑वि॒वेश॒ भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑
प्र॒जाप॑तिः प्र॒जया॑ सᳪररा॒णस्त्रीणि॒ ज्योती॑ᳪषि सचते॒ स षो॑डशी

pra̱jāpa̭tiḥ pra̱jayā̭ saᳪrarā̱ṇastrīṇi̱ jyotī̭ᳪṣi sacate̱ sa ṣo̭ḍaśī

hindi: इन्द्र और सम्राट् वरुण राजा, उन दोनों ने पहले तुम्हारे लिए यह भक्ष बनाया। उन दोनों के पीछे मैं भक्ष का भक्षण करता हूँ; वाग्देवी सेवन करती हुई सोम से तृप्त हो, प्राण के साथ। स्वाहा।
english: Indra, and Varuṇa the supreme ruler and king: those two made this portion for you at first. After those two I partake of the portion; may the goddess Speech, enjoying, be satisfied with the Soma, together with the breath. Svāhā.

english: I shake you in the flight of the Vreśīs; I shake you in the flight of the Kukūnanas; I shake you in the flight of the exulting ones; I shake you in the flight of the most intoxicating ones; I shake you in the flight of the sweetest ones. english: You two, O Indra and Parvata, fighters in front: whoever would fight against us, strike away him, him indeed; with the thunderbolt strike him, him indeed. notes: List of names each paired with a state participle, with no verbs; the line does not say what the names stand for. 'āprītapā' is obscure (kept as a transliteration). 'kṣīra-śrīḥ' and 'saktu-śrīḥ' read as 'mixed with milk / with barley meal' (√śrī); 'manthī' read as 'manthin', a mixed drink or its name. 'aṃśu' is left untranslated.

hindi: सब देव चमसों में ऊपर उठाए हुए; असु होम के लिए उठाया हुआ; रुद्र आहुति दिया जाता हुआ; वात अभिमुख हुआ; नृचक्षा प्रख्यात। भक्ष भक्षण किया जाता हुआ; पितर नाराशंस।
english: All the gods, taken up in the cups; the life-breath, lifted up for the oblation; Rudra, being offered; Vāta, turned toward; Nṛcakṣas, regarded; the portion, being partaken; the Fathers, the Nārāśaṃsas.
notes: List of names paired with participles, no verbs. 'asuḥ' read as life-breath (not 'asura'); 'nṛcakṣāḥ' kept as a name with a literal gloss; 'nārāśaṃsāḥ' kept in Sanskrit. 'pratikhyātaḥ' rendered 'regarded' (or 'named'). The sense of the pairs is not given by the line.

hindi: बैठा हुआ; सिन्धु अवभृथ के लिए उठाया हुआ; समुद्र नीचे ले जाया जाता हुआ; सलिल बहता हुआ। जिन दोनों के बल से अन्तरिक्ष के क्षेत्र थामे गए, जो अपने वीर कर्मों से अत्यन्त वीर और सबसे बलवान हैं; जो दोनों अपने बलों से अप्रतिहत होकर स्वामित्व करते हैं, वे विष्णु और वरुण पहली पुकार पर आए।
english: Settled; the river, lifted up for the avabhṛtha; the sea, being carried down; the water, flooding forth. They two by whose strength the airy realms were propped, most heroic by their heroic deeds, the strongest; they two who rule unopposed with their powers, Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, came at the first invocation.
notes: GROUPING: 'sannaḥ' (first word) probably belongs with the end of unit 58 ('pitaro nārāśaṃsāḥ sannaḥ'), since the list pairs names with participles; the edition's division is kept. Lines 2 and 3 are a verse; 'viṣṇū' and 'varuṇā' are dual-looking forms read as 'Viṣṇu and Varuṇa' (the two named as a pair is uncertain). 'agan' (3 sg. root aorist) stands with the two as subject. 'rajāṃsi' rendered 'airy realms' (or 'worlds').
lines_deva: स॒न्नः सिन्धु॑रवभृ॒थायोद्य॑तः समु॒द्रो॒ऽभ्यवह्रि॒यमा॑णः स॑लि॒लः प्रप्लु॑तो
ययो॒रोज॑सा स्कभि॒ता रजा॑ᳪसि वी॒र्ये॑भिर्वी॒रत॑मा॒ शवि॑ष्ठा
या पत्ये॑ते॒ अप्र॑तीता॒ सहो॑भि॒र्विष्णू॑ अग॒न्वरु॑णा पू॒र्वहू॑तौ

yayo̱roja̭sā skabhi̱tā rajā̭ᳪsi vī̱ryḙbhirvī̱rata̭mā̱ śavi̭ṣṭhā

hindi: यज्ञ देवों के पास, स्वर्ग को गया है; उससे मुझे धन प्राप्त हो। यज्ञ मनुष्यों के पास, अन्तरिक्ष को गया है; उससे मुझे धन प्राप्त हो। यज्ञ पितरों के पास, पृथ्वी को गया है; उससे मुझे धन प्राप्त हो। यज्ञ जिस किसी लोक को गया है, उससे मेरा कल्याण हुआ है।
english: The sacrifice has gone to the gods, to heaven; from that may wealth reach me. The sacrifice has gone to men, to the atmosphere; from that may wealth reach me. The sacrifice has gone to the Fathers, to the earth; from that may wealth reach me. To whatever world the sacrifice has gone, from that good has come to me.
notes: 'devān divam agan yajñaḥ' read as 'the sacrifice has gone to the gods, to heaven' (the pairing of each group with its realm is the line's own). 'aṣṭu' from √aś (reach). 'bhadraṃma̭bhūt' = bhadram + abhūt. The printed 'bhadraṃm abhūt' has an extra ṃ before m (expected bhadram abhūt); possibly the edition's own spelling, kept as printed.
lines_deva: दे॒वान्दिव॑मगन्य॒ज्ञस्ततो॑ मा॒ द्रवि॑णमष्टु मनु॒ष्या॒न॒न्तरि॑क्षमगन्य॒ज्ञस्ततो॑ मा॒ द्रवि॑णमष्टु
पि॒तॄन्पृ॑थि॒वीम॑गन्य॒ज्ञस्ततो॑ मा॒ द्रवि॑णमष्टु॒ यं कं च॑ लो॒कमग॑न्य॒ज्ञस्ततो॑ मे भ॒द्रंम॑भूत्

hindi: जो चौंतीस तन्तु फैलाए गए हैं, जो इस यज्ञ को स्वधा के साथ देते हैं, उनका जो कटा हुआ है, उसे मैं जोड़कर रखता हूँ। स्वाहा। घर्म देवों के पास जाए।
english: The thirty-four threads that have been stretched out, which give this sacrifice with svadhā: what is severed of them I put together. Svāhā. May the hot offering go to the gods.
notes: 'samvetaddadhāmi' is read sam + u + etat + dadhāmi (the u becoming v before a vowel); 'sam etat' with a different second element is possible, so this is tentative. 'dadante' (give) takes the sacrifice as object; the threads are not identified. 'chinna' = severed.
lines_deva: चतु॑स्त्रिᳪश॒त्तन्त॑वो॒ ये वित॑त्नि॒रे य इ॒मं य॒ज्ञᳪ स्व॒धया॒ दद॑न्ते
तेषां॑ छि॒न्नᳪ सम्वे॒तद्द॑धामि॒ स्वाहा॑ घ॒र्मो अप्ये॑तु दे॒वान्

hindi: यज्ञ का दोह अनेक स्थानों में फैला हुआ है; उसने आठ प्रकार से स्वर्ग के साथ-साथ विस्तार किया। हे यज्ञ, वह तू मेरे लिए बहुत दुह: प्रजा में धन की पुष्टि; मैं पूर्ण आयु प्राप्त करूँ। स्वाहा।
english: The yield of the sacrifice is spread out in many places; he stretched eightfold along heaven. That you, O sacrifice, yield greatly for me in offspring an increase of wealth; may I attain the full life. Svāhā.

text_flags.why: possible: stray space inside prajāyām (loc. sg.), before rāyaspoṣam; the Devanagari has the same split

notes: 'saḥ' in line 1 is 'he' (the sacrifice or its yield; not stated). 'mahi' may be 'greatly' or an adjective with the yield; 'prajāyām' read as locative 'in offspring' (the stray space splits the word).

english: Flow clear hither, O Soma, with gold, with horses, with heroes; bring strength rich in cattle. Svāhā.
notes: 'pavasva' (√pū) is rendered 'flow clear'; 'hiraṇya-vat' etc. are adverbial '-vat' forms ('endowed with'). The line has the first half-verse and the second half-verse, ending with svāhā.
